ABSTRACT
The effect of CuO and MnO2 as sintering additives on the structural, ferroelectric, and magnetic properties of 0:7BiFeO30:3(Ba0:85Ca0:15)TiO3
was investigated. The addition of CuO can inhibit grain growth, and the sample possesses the maximum remanent magnetization. However,
the addition of MnO2 can promote grain growth, and the sample exhibits the maximum remanent polarization of 34 μC=cm2. Nevertheless,
the addition of both CuO and MnO2 can markedly enhance the magnetic properties. The magnetization measurements manifest that all the
samples undergo a paramagnetic to ferrimagnetic transition arising from the existence of a net moment due to the antiferrimagnetic interac-
tions between Fe2þ and Fe3þ sublattices. The enhanced magnetism of the samples with the addition of CuO and MnO2 can be due to the
enhanced superexchange interaction between Fe2þ and Fe3þ arising from the increased Fe–O–Fe bond angle.

Multiferroic materials, which combine order parameters like 
magnetic, electric, and structural, showing the simultaneous pre­
sence of ferromagnetic, ferroelectric, and ferroelastic phenomena, 
have recently attracted interest in creating multifunctional devices 
[11]. These materials display coexisting ferromagnetism, ferroelec­
tricity, and ferroelasticity in at least two ferroic orders in a single 
phase [12]. Research into multiferroic materials has increased as a 
result of the identification of magnetoelectric interaction in systems 
like BiFeO3 and TbMnO3 [13,14]. Because multiferroic composites 
have a significantly stronger magnetoelectric (ME) effect at room 
temperature than single-phase materials, they have attracted re­
searchers' attention for a variety of device applications, including 
actuators, sensors, and memory devices [15,16].
BiFeO3 (BFO) is a typical single-phase multiferroic compound 
that has attracted a lot of interest among other multiferroic mate­
rials due to the high temperature of ferroelectric and anti­
ferromagnetic ordering [17]. It is also a very suitable candidate for 
room temperature application. BFO exhibits ferroelectricity as well 
as G-type anti-ferromagnetism with Curie temperature (TC) and Neel 
temperatures (TN) at 1103 K and 643 K respectively, and has a dis­
torted rhombohedral perovskite structure with R3c space group 
symmetry at room temperature [18]. Ferroelectricity is produced by 
the displacement of Bi3+ ions from central-symmetric positions in 
relation to the oxygen ions around them, while the magnetic spins of 
unpaired Fe3+ ions are responsible for magnetism [19,20]. Despite its 
many intriguing aspects, the BFO has some drawbacks, including 
secondary phase formation, weak magnetoelectric coupling, poor 
magnetization, enhanced dielectric loss, high leakage current, and 
weak ferroelectric reliability [21]. Two approaches can be used to 
overcome all of these issues. The first approach is to make compo­
sites of solid solutions with other perovskites (e.g., ferroelectric 
PbTiO3, BaTiO3, and SrTiO3) to improve the resistance to electric 
insulation and stabilize the perovskite structure [22]. The second 
method is to partially substitute rare-earth ions (Nd3+, Y3+, Gd3+, 
Sm3+, Dy3+, etc.) at the A site of BFO to improve magnetic char­
acteristics [23–25]. It has been demonstrated that the co-substitu­
tion of the A and B sites enhances the multiferroic properties of BFO 
in bulk ceramics and thin films [26–28]. Furthermore, doping the A 
and B sites with off-valent ions separately or simultaneously will 
help reduce oxygen vacancies without changing the ionic state of 
Fe3+ and lead to FeO6 octahedra distortion and suppression of in­
homogeneous magnetic spin structure.
The formation of solid solutions with Perovskite-type materials 
like PbTiO3 or BaTiO3, which improve optical and multiferroic 
properties, has been mentioned in numerous literary works in recent 
years [17,29]. Pradhan et al. investigated the multiferroic properties 
of a La-modified (BiFeO3)1-x(PbTiO3)x system, as evidenced by mea­
surements of ferroelectric loops and magnetoelectric coefficient 
[30]. Other binary multiferroic perovskites were studied in previous 
work to determine structural, magnetic, piezoelectric, and optical 
properties, and multiferroic properties were found to be greatly 
improved [31]. The PbTiO3 (PTO) is used due to its high polarization 
and dielectric constant ferroelectric material, which settles the 
perovskite phase of the composite and creates a morphotropic phase 
boundary (MPB) with BFO due to the difference in crystal symmetry 
between PTO and BFO. Furthermore, we developed a BFO-PTO solid 
solution to reduce leakage current and improve the functional 
properties of BFO. The BFO-PTO composite can be viewed as a fusion 
of ferroelectric and piezoelectric components that are frequently 
employed in the industry for memory, sensors, and actuators [32].
Furthermore, doping in BFO with the rare earth element gado­
linium (Gd) improved its multiferroic properties, as well as the 
magnetic ordering of Dy-doped BFO is improved by the effective 
magnetic moment of the Dy ion concentration [33,34]. Considering 
the preceding, it is reasonable to replace Bi3+ ion with a rare earth 
ion of small ionic radius and large magnetic moment equivalently to 
improve the multiferroic characteristics of BFO. Moreover, dielectric 
ceramics are regarded as one kind of prospective candidate for next- 
generation pulsed-power capacitors owing to their environmental 
friendliness and relatively high energy storage performance [35]. 
Among the dielectric ceramics, lead (Pb)-based ceramics dominated 
the market due to exceptional energy storage properties (ESPs) in 
recent decades. Relaxor ferroelectrics are considered excellent can­
didates for high energy storage applications because their slim 
hysteresis loops, large maximum polarization (Pmax), small remnant 
polarization (Pr), and moderate breakdown strength (Eb) result in 
high recoverable energy storage density (Wrec) and efficiency (η). For 
example, Ogihara et al. first introduced Bi3+ and Sc3+ to replace the 
Ba2+ in the A-site and Ti4+ in the B-site simultaneously, forming 
weakly coupled ceramics, and an improved Wrec of 2.3 Jcm−3 was 
obtained in 0.7BaTiO3–0.3BiScO3 [36]. Zuo et al. synthesized NaN­
bO3–Bi(Mg0.5Ti0.5)O3 ceramics, achieving a large Wrec of 5.57 Jcm−3 
and η of 71 % simultaneously [37]. Wang et al. realized excellent Wrec 
(7.5 Jcm−3) and η (92 %) in 0.62Na0.5Bi0.5TiO3–0.3Sr0.7Bi0.2TiO3 
–0.08BiMg2/3Nb1/3O3 (NBT-SBT-0.08BMN) at 470 kV cm−1 [38]. In 
addition, rare earth element doped BFO has been shown to improve 
multiferroic properties in the literature, but no systematic in­
vestigation of the magnetoelectric, piezoelectric, and energy storage 
properties of bulk Nd doped BFO-PTO solid solution has been con­
ducted. In this study, the crystalline samples of (BNFPT)x with 
varying x compositions are synthesized via solid-state reaction 
technique. The structural, multiferroic, and energy storage proper­
ties of (BNFPT)x with differing x compositions are explored in detail. 
The effect of Nd doping on leakage current and the piezoelectric 
effect was also investigated.
